rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one forcing function with no fence is the diff push-back (## Read the diff and push back on a line, L24-27): no {{prompt:}} block, pure body prose. Harm the rule guards against: a speed-runner reading fences only would skip a scripted-count nicety, but here skipping the beat skips the exercise's stated point (L9: "pushing back is core work"). This is a documented maintainer accept-note, not an oversight: maintainer block L56 ("the compound-step mention in the push-back bullet stays") and backing Stance ("the student writes their own push-back with no prompt supplied, which is slower and worse-scaffolded on purpose, because the words have to be theirs when the compound step reuses them") give the design reason — a fence would hand the student a template instead of forcing their own wording. The Ship-the-PR beat (L47-49) is the same shape, and the maintainer block's Prompt progression note (L74) names it explicitly as "intentionally prose-led, not a fenced prompt block" since the student is already in the repo with the fixed diff in context. Both are covered accept-notes, not silent violations.
